title: Two kinds of API
subtitle: The code a page runs is a release that never changes; the server it talks to is a deployment. Inês pins one and runs the other. 8 panels.
rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's, not a quote, and is marked not_a_quote; evidence panels quote this site's pages word for word, which the build checks.

scenes.title: Two kinds of API
scenes.subtitle: Files a page runs, and a server it talks to.
scenes.note: The contradiction Dinis found after the first deploy, and the rule that came out of it.

scenes.caption: Which release?

cast.says: Which release is this page running?

scenes.note: A page names one release by its full address and copies its manifest.

scenes.caption: A release is a folder that never changes

lines: a change is the next folder,
never an edit of this one

scenes.note: Every minor release is a complete, independent copy; the gate fails a hash that moved.

scenes.caption: The server is a deployment
scenes.note: One HTTP contract, many deployments; the page names the one it talks to as an endpoint.

scenes.caption: Her own server

cast.says: Mine. On my laptop. Nothing leaves it.

scenes.note: The in-memory server in every API release: the same routes, for tests and for a laptop.

scenes.caption: The rule
scenes.note: The order of the labels does the work; one sentence to explain.

scenes.caption: Contract versus deployment

evidence.quote: The distinction is contract versus deployment, not JavaScript versus Python.

scenes.note: Quoted from the article, word for word.

scenes.punchline: Pin the files. Name the server. Never confuse the two.
scenes.note: Decided on 20 October 2026; not yet deployed as new hosts.
